The second pathway links Oxostephamiersine to (6aR,11aR)-9-hydroxy-3-methoxy-6a,11a-dihydro-6H-[1]benzofuro[3,2-c]chromene-2-carbaldehyde, which also targets UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4, reinforcing the role of this enzyme in the metabolic pathway. The third pathway shows Oxostephamiersine interacting with CWR22R, which is a target of Mycalenitrile 13, further supporting the involvement of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4 in the downstream effects of these compounds. These findings collectively suggest that Oxostephamiersine may modulate UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4 through multiple mechanisms, potentially influencing drug metabolism or cellular processes.
